verses.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
verses.2: In you, O LORD, I have placed my trust. I will not be put to shame for all time. In your righteousness, rescue me.
verses.3: Incline your ear to me quickly, and deliver me. Be to me a strong rock, a fortress of safety to save me.
verses.4: For you are my rock and my fortress. Because of your name, lead me and guide me.
verses.5: Rescue me from this trap they have set for me, for you are my protector.
verses.6: Into your hands I commit my spirit. You, O LORD, the faithful God, have redeemed me.
verses.7: I hate those who cling to worthless things and empty promises. But I have placed my trust in the LORD.
verses.8: I will rejoice and be glad in your steadfast love, for you saw my distress and rescued me from my troubles.
verses.9: You did not hand me over to the power of the enemy. You have set my feet in a broad place.
verses.10: Have mercy on me, O LORD, for I am in distress. My eyes are troubled by anger; my soul and my body are weary.
verses.11: For my life has passed in sorrow, and my years in sighing. My strength has failed in affliction, and my bones have grown feeble.
verses.12: I have become a disgrace to all my enemies and a horror to my neighbors. My known companions have fled from me in fear.
verses.13: I have been forgotten as if dead. I have become like a broken vessel.
verses.14: For I have heard the talk of many who surround me. When they conspired together against me to take my life, they plotted.
verses.15: But I have trusted in you, O LORD. I have said, "You are my God."
verses.16: My times are in your hands. Deliver me from the hands of my enemies and from those who pursue me.
verses.17: Show your face upon your servant. Save me in your steadfast love.
verses.18: O LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I have called on you. Let the wicked be put to shame, and be silent in Sheol.
verses.19: Let the lips of the deceitful be silent, the words of the wicked that accuse the righteous in arrogance and deceit be done away.
verses.20: How great is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you, done for those who trust in you in the sight of the children of men.
verses.21: You will hide them in the shelter of your presence from the troubles of men; you will keep them in a tent from the strife of tongues.
verses.22: Praise be to the LORD, for he has shown me his steadfast love in a city of siege.
verses.23: And I said in my distress, "I have been rejected from before your eyes." But you, O LORD, heard the voice of my plea when I cried out to you.
verses.24: Let all your faithful ones love you, O LORD. The LORD is faithful and rewards those who act with excess pride.
verses.25: Be strong, and let your hearts be steadfast, all you who wait for the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "For the choir director" reflects the traditional reading of "lamnatzeach" as a musical instruction.
- v. 20: "done for those who trust in you" captures the sense of poetic action (pe'al) rather than passive construction.
- v. 24: "rewards those who act with excess pride" reflects the poetic justice theme in "ve-mesaleim al-yeter oseh gav'awa" with a slight interpretive nuance for clarity.

[1] For the choir director. A psalm of David.

[2] In you, O LORD, I have placed my trust. I will not be put to shame for all time. In your righteousness, rescue me.

[3] Incline your ear to me quickly, and deliver me. Be to me a strong rock, a fortress of safety to save me.

[4] For you are my rock and my fortress. Because of your name, lead me and guide me.

[5] Rescue me from this trap they have set for me, for you are my protector.

[6] Into your hands I commit my spirit. You, O LORD, the faithful God, have redeemed me.

[7] I hate those who cling to worthless things and empty promises. But I have placed my trust in the LORD.

[8] I will rejoice and be glad in your steadfast love, for you saw my distress and rescued me from my troubles.

[9] You did not hand me over to the power of the enemy. You have set my feet in a broad place.

[10] Have mercy on me, O LORD, for I am in distress. My eyes are troubled by anger; my soul and my body are weary.

[11] For my life has passed in sorrow, and my years in sighing. My strength has failed in affliction, and my bones have grown feeble.

[12] I have become a disgrace to all my enemies and a horror to my neighbors. My known companions have fled from me in fear.

[13] I have been forgotten as if dead. I have become like a broken vessel.

[14] For I have heard the talk of many who surround me. When they conspired together against me to take my life, they plotted.

[15] But I have trusted in you, O LORD. I have said, "You are my God."

[16] My times are in your hands. Deliver me from the hands of my enemies and from those who pursue me.

[17] Show your face upon your servant. Save me in your steadfast love.

[18] O LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I have called on you. Let the wicked be put to shame, and be silent in Sheol.

[19] Let the lips of the deceitful be silent, the words of the wicked that accuse the righteous in arrogance and deceit be done away.

[20] How great is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you, done for those who trust in you in the sight of the children of men.

[21] You will hide them in the shelter of your presence from the troubles of men; you will keep them in a tent from the strife of tongues.

[22] Praise be to the LORD, for he has shown me his steadfast love in a city of siege.

[23] And I said in my distress, "I have been rejected from before your eyes." But you, O LORD, heard the voice of my plea when I cried out to you.

[24] Let all your faithful ones love you, O LORD. The LORD is faithful and rewards those who act with excess pride.

[25] Be strong, and let your hearts be steadfast, all you who wait for the LORD.

Notes
- v. 1: "For the choir director" reflects the traditional reading of "lamnatzeach" as a musical instruction.
- v. 20: "done for those who trust in you" captures the sense of poetic action (pe'al) rather than passive construction.
- v. 24: "rewards those who act with excess pride" reflects the poetic justice theme in "ve-mesaleim al-yeter oseh gav'awa" with a slight interpretive nuance for clarity.
